issues.legal_issue: A thekदार acquires hereditary-tenant status when the land is personally cultivated on the qualifying day under a theka made for the thekदार’s personal cultivation.
material_facts: The plaintiffs were thekadars and were found to have personally cultivated the disputed land for eleven years, including on the qualifying day.
The last fact-finding court found that the theka was for personal cultivation and that the thekadars had no other duties, such as collecting rent from other tenants.
The thekadars sought possession after the landholders inducted other occupants.
issues.conclusion: The thekadars acquired hereditary-tenant status and were entitled to hold the land and recover possession of it.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12(1) of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950 deems a thekदार who personally cultivated the land on the qualifying day under a theka made for personal cultivation to be a hereditary tenant, entitled to hold the land and regain possession if ejected. Babu Noorul Hasan Khan v. Ram Prasad Singh and Raghunandan Singh v. Brij Mohan Singh establish that personal cultivation incidental to a thekदार’s other duties is insufficient; the theka must be made for personal cultivation.

rule.if: land_possession_recovery_proceeding and claimant_is_thekदार and personally_cultivating_on_qualifying_day and theka_made_for_personal_cultivation

predicates.land_possession_recovery_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a thekदार seeking recovery of agricultural land from persons inducted by a landholder.
predicates.claimant_is_thekदार: The claimant held the land under a theka as a thekदार.
predicates.personally_cultivating_on_qualifying_day: The thekदार personally cultivated the land on the legally qualifying day.
predicates.theka_made_for_personal_cultivation: The theka was made for the thekदार’s personal cultivation, rather than for other duties with cultivation merely incidental.

issues.definition: When a thekदार seeking recovery of land personally cultivated it on the qualifying day under a theka made for that purpose, the thekदार acquires hereditary-tenant status.

issues.legal_issue: Cultivatory possession obtained under a landholder who had no right to induct the occupant does not qualify as lawful possession for acquiring statutory occupancy status.
material_facts: The thekadars had acquired hereditary-tenant rights and were in possession of the disputed land.
The landholders inducted the lessees after they no longer had the right to grant possession against the thekadars.
The lessees claimed occupancy status based on cultivatory possession during the relevant agricultural year, but their possession was unlawful against the thekadars.
issues.conclusion: The lessees did not acquire adhivasi rights because their cultivatory possession was not lawful; the hereditary tenants were entitled to a decree for possession.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3 of the U.P. Land Reforms (Supplementary) Act, 1952 requires lawful cultivatory possession for the relevant year to acquire the claimed status. Sonawati v. Shri Ram holds that a person must have a lawful right to possession and that forcible or wrongful occupation does not qualify; Ram Krishna v. Bhagwan Baksh Singh is consistent with that principle. The Court rejected the contrary view in Nanhoo Mai v. Muloo.

rule.if: land_possession_recovery_proceeding and occupancy_status_claim_based_on_cultivation and cultivatory_possession_during_qualifying_year and prior_tenant_had_acquired_rights and landholder_inducted_claimant_after_losing_right and not possession_lawful

predicates.land_possession_recovery_proceeding: The proceeding concerns recovery of agricultural land from an occupant claiming a statutory occupancy status.
predicates.occupancy_status_claim_based_on_cultivat: The occupant claims statutory status on the basis of cultivatory possession.
predicates.cultivatory_possession_during_qualifying: The occupant was in cultivatory possession during the relevant agricultural year.
predicates.prior_tenant_had_acquired_rights: A prior cultivating tenant had acquired rights to the land before the occupant was inducted.
predicates.landholder_inducted_claimant_after_losin: The landholder inducted the occupant after losing the right to grant possession against the prior tenant.
predicates.possession_lawful: The occupant's possession was supported by a lawful right against the prior tenant.

issues.definition: An occupant who claims status based on cultivatory possession during the relevant year does not acquire that status when the prior tenant already had rights, the landholder inducted the occupant after losing the right to do so, and the occupant's possession was not lawful.
